Bug_Details:
DoubleMath.fuzzyEquals should never be used in an Object.equals() method From documentation: DoubleMath.fuzzyEquals is not transitive, so it is not
suitable for use in Object#equals implementations.
Bug_Explanation: The bug occurs when DoubleMath.fuzzyEquals method is used in the equals method. This method is not transitive and is not suitable for use in Object#equals implementations. It's a part of the Google Guava library.

Trigger_Explanation: This JUNIT test case triggers the bug because it uses DoubleMath.fuzzyEquals in the equals method, which is not suitable for use in Object#equals implementations. The DoubleMath.fuzzyEquals method is not transitive, hence, the test will fail at the bug.
Model_Explanation: The bug is present in the code. The DoubleMath.fuzzyEquals method is used in the equals method of the FuzzyEqualsObject class. This method is not suitable for use in Object#equals implementations because it is not transitive. This means that if a.equals(b) and b.equals(c), it does not necessarily mean that a.equals(c). In this case, the fuzzyEquals method is used with a tolerance of 0.001, which means that two numbers are considered equal if they are within 0.001 of each other. This can lead to unexpected results, as shown in the showBug method where obj1 and obj2 are considered equal, even though they are not.
